patient_summary:
Hello there! I'm here to explain what the doctor found during your ultrasound test and what you need to do next. 

You had a test done to check your carotid arteries, which are the main blood vessels in your neck that carry blood to your brain. Your doctor was concerned about a headache you've been having, so they wanted to make sure everything was okay.

The test showed that both of your carotid arteries looked okay. The right side had some small thickening, but nothing serious. The left side had more thickening and some hard plaque, which is like a buildup of material on the inside of the artery. This is a bit concerning because it can lead to problems if it gets too big.

The doctor also noticed that the left side had a bit of a blockage, but it wasn't very big. They want to check this more closely with another test called a CT angiogram (CTA). This is to make sure there's no bigger problem that they might not have seen with just the ultrasound.

For now, you don't need to take any special medicines. The doctor will talk to you about what to do next. If you have any more headaches or if you feel dizzy or confused, you should tell your doctor right away. They can help you feel better.

Remember, it's important to follow the doctor's advice and keep them updated about how you're feeling. You're doing great!
caregiver_checklist: Give the patient a pain reliever as needed for headache, following the prescribed dose.
Check the patient’s blood pressure regularly, as high blood pressure can affect carotid arteries.
Watch for signs of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), such as sudden numbness, weakness, confusion, trouble speaking, or vision changes.
Call 911 if the patient has a severe headache, especially if it is the first time they have had a headache.
Schedule a follow-up appointment with the neurologist or cardiologist to discuss the findings and next steps.
Check the patient’s blood pressure at home and record it for the next visit.
Watch for any new or worsening symptoms of stroke or TIA.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient experiences any new or concerning symptoms.
Schedule a CT angiography (CTA) scan for the left internal carotid artery to assess the stenosis further.
child_explanation: You had a special check-up for your head. The doctors looked at your neck with a machine. They saw some spots that aren't as smooth. But don't worry, it's like when you get a small cut. The doctors and grown-ups are taking good care of you. They might need to look at your neck again with a different machine. You'll be okay, you're in good hands.
source_text: EXAM:,  Bilateral carotid ultrasound.,REASON FOR EXAM: , Headache.,TECHNIQUE:  ,Color grayscale and Doppler analysis is employed.,FINDINGS:,  On the grayscale images, the right common carotid artery demonstrates patency with mild intimal thickening only.  At the level of the carotid bifurcation, there is heterogeneous hard plaque present, but without grayscale evidence of greater than 50% stenosis.  Right common carotid waveform is normal with a peak systolic velocity of 0.474 m/second and an end-diastolic velocity of 0.131 m/second.  The right ECA is patent as well with the velocity measurement 0.910 m/second.,The right internal carotid artery at the bifurcation demonstrates plaque formation, but no evidence of greater than 50% stenosis.  Proximal peak systolic velocity in the internal carotid artery is 0.463 m/second with proximal end-diastolic velocity of 0.170.  The mid internal carotid peak systolic velocity is 0.564 m/second, and mid ICA end-diastolic velocity is 0.199 m/second.  Right ICA distal PSV 0.580 m/second, right ICA distal EDV 0.204 m/second.  Vertebral flow is antegrade on the right at 0.469 m/second.,On the left, the common carotid artery demonstrates intimal thickening, but is otherwise patent.  At the level of the bifurcation, however, there is more pronounced plaque formation with approximately 50% stenosis by the grayscale analysis.  See the velocity measurements below:,Left carotid ECA measurement 0.938 m/second.  Left common carotid PSV 0.686 m/second, and left common carotid end-diastolic velocity 0.137 m/second.,Left internal carotid artery again demonstrates prominent focus of hard plaque with up to at least 50% stenosis.  This should be further assessed with CTA for more precise measurement.  The left proximal ICA/PSV 0.955 m/second, left proximal ICA/EDV 0.287 m/second.  There is spectral broadening in the proximal aspect of the carotid waveform.  The left carotid ICA mid PSV 0.895, left carotid ICA mid EDV 0.278 with also spectral broadening present.,The left distal ICA/PSV 0.561, left distal ICA/EDV 0.206, again the spectral broadening present.  Vertebral flow is antegrade at 0.468 m/second.,IMPRESSION: , The study demonstrates bilateral hard plaque at the bifurcation, left greater than right.  There is at least 50% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery at its bifurcation and a followup CTA is recommended for further assessment.
